_comment: Build config for the `publisher` cron service. Same repo and same root directory as the API,
so it needs its own file rather than its own directory — the service points at this path via
Two differences from railway.json, both because a cron run is a process that finishes:
- no healthcheck. `/health` belongs to a server that keeps listening; a cron container exits
as soon as the cycle is done, so a healthcheck would fail every successful run.
- restartPolicyType NEVER. A finished run must not be restarted — the schedule is what starts
the next one, and a restart loop would publish repeatedly. A failed cycle is left failed and
the next tick retries it; `run_once` already absorbs per-post failures.
The start command overrides the Dockerfile's CMD (migrate + serve). Migrations stay with the
API: two services racing `alembic upgrade head` on the same database is a lock, not a feature.
